name: Sulfur spot treatment (Mario Badescu Drying Lotion)

card.summary: A pink overnight spot treatment, combining calamine, sulfur and salicylic acid, that people dab on pimples to dry them out and flatten them.
card.note: Contains drying alcohol; apply only to individual blemishes.

quick.overview:
Mario Badescu Drying Lotion is a cult pink spot treatment for whiteheads and surface blemishes. It combines calamine and zinc oxide with sulfur and salicylic acid, ingredients associated with drying out and clearing pimples.

Formulated by chemist Mario Badescu in the 1960s, it gained a social media following, with the brand-linked hashtag reportedly passing 100 million TikTok views. Dermatologists quoted by Bustle describe it as a spot treatment for use in a pinch.
quick.how: Users dip a cotton swab into the settled pink sediment and tap it on an individual pimple, often at night, leaving it as a "tiny pink mask" and removing it in the morning. The bottle has two layers and the brand advises against shaking it.
quick.risks: Dermatologists quoted by Bustle say drying agents can irritate skin, so it is applied only to the blemish and used periodically. It contains isopropyl alcohol, which can be drying or stinging on sensitive skin.

lead: Mario Badescu Drying Lotion is a pink, two-phase spot treatment sold for whiteheads and surface blemishes. Users dab the pink sediment on a pimple, often overnight, to make it look smaller and drier by morning.[1]

The lotion was first formulated in the 1960s by Mario Badescu, a chemist and pharmacist who moved to New York from Vienna.[1] Its ingredients include calamine, sulfur, zinc oxide, talc and salicylic acid in an alcohol and water base, as listed by retailers. Calamine is a zinc oxide and iron oxide preparation used to relieve itching and dry weeping skin.[2]

Dermatologist Marisa Garshick told Bustle it can quickly dry up a breakout and is best used in a pinch, and Leah Ansell said sulfur and salicylic acid target acne while the drying agents dry it out.[1] Celebrity mentions and TikTok helped make it a staple of spot-treatment routines.[1]

chain: Drying agents and sulfur act overnight
angle.text: People use it to shrink and dry individual pimples ahead of the next day, putting it on only the spot and leaving it overnight.

infobox: Calamine, sulfur, zinc oxide, salicylic acid, isopropyl alcohol

paras: The product is a bi-phase liquid whose pink sediment settles under a clear layer. The brand advises letting the layers separate and applying a swab dipped to the sediment, tapped onto the pimple only.[1]

Retailers list isopropyl alcohol, water, calamine, camphor, sulfur, zinc oxide, talc, glycerin, salicylic acid and titanium dioxide. Calamine is zinc oxide with a small amount of iron oxide and is used topically for itching and to dry weeping skin; some people use it for acne, and it can damage the barrier of sensitive skin.[2] Dermatologist Leah Ansell said the combination helps offset irritation from some ingredients.[1]
Celebrities including Bella Hadid and Jennifer Aniston have praised it, and the hashtag reportedly has over 107 million TikTok views.[1]
No studies found of this specific product. Calamine is on the World Health Organization list of essential medicines for skin use.[2]

Dermatologists quoted by Bustle note the drying agents can irritate skin and recommend applying to the pimple only and using periodically.[1] It is described as suited to surface whiteheads rather than deep cystic acne.[1]

timeline.event: Mario Badescu first formulates the Drying Lotion.[1]
